newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dow makes $446 million bid for Sentrachem Ltd.
newsitem.headline: Dow makes $446 million bid for Sentrachem Ltd.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said Monday it would seek to buy South African chemical manufacturer Sentrachem Ltd in a deal valued at $446 million.
The offer, which is subject to the approval of Sentrachem's shareholders, has already been approved by investment firm Sankorp Ltd, which holds a 39 percent stake in Sentrachem.
Sentrachem, with annual sales of 5.5 billion rand ($1.18 billion), makes speciality and agricultural chemicals, as well as polypropylene, polyethylene, latex and rubber products.
Midland, Mich.-based Dow first entered the South African market in 1959, but pulled out during the 1980s as firms faced pressure to disinvest from the former white-ruled state.

However, the chemical giant returned to South Africa after an eight-year absence in 1995, a year after the country's first fully democratic elections, to operate a polyurethane plant near Durban on the Indian Ocean coast.

"This acquisition reinforces our strategic direction to enhance Dow's performance-chemicals portfolio with the addition of Sentrachem's strong speciality and agricultural chemicals businesses, among others," said Dow President William Stavropoulos.
Dow is the world's fifth-largest chemical company, with 40,000 employees and annual sales of more than $20 billion.

Sentrachem has been going through a troubled period recently. It embarked on a huge restructuring plan in June after posting a pre-tax loss of 257 million rand ($55.3 million) in the first half of 1997.
If the Dow purchase goes through as expected, some elements of the restructuring are likely to come under review, the company said.
Sentrachem's stock was halted Monday on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange pending an announcement, but analysts said investors were likely to applaud the deal.
"It is about time Sentrachem came out with some good news," said Peer Ieul, managing director at UAL Securities.
Dow Chemical's stock was down 37.5 cents at $93.69 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
